subject: Level-number
notes: kb/Work PB836 LANDED; kb/Work PB981 LANDED (determination D-FRA, docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3). Sentence 1 - 'Multiple level 1 entries subordinate to a FD or SD entry represent implicit redefinitions of the same area': DataBinder.LinkImplicitRecordArea, the ONE linker for the FD and SD arms, joins every later CHARACTER-WINDOW level-1 record to the first through DataItem.SetRedefinition(first, RedefinitionKind.ImplicitFileRecord); the storage layout reads the one class for both constructs, while the 13.18.44.3 REDEFINES-clause screens read RedefinesKind == Clause only. Since PB981 a dynamic-length record, a variable-length group or a pointer-class record - legal source that used to be staged loud as COBOL0899 - is an OUT-OF-LINE record (FileModel.IsOutOfLineRecord): 8.5.1.10.3 lets its storage be located elsewhere, so it is never linked into the class and shares the area at the transfer boundary instead - a READ/RETURN makes the current record available in it (SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRecordAreaStore; a variable-length group through the one split rule CobolVarGroup.FromContiguous), and a WRITE/REWRITE/RELEASE sends its contiguous image (8.5.1.11.2). The 2014 golden writes and reads back a variable-length group, a dynamic-length record and a character record of one FD, a SAME RECORD AREA peer and an SD; the 2002 golden a pointer record beside a character record. Residue stated in D-FRA: an EXTERNAL file whose area has an out-of-line record, and a SORT/MERGE key that follows a variable-length member, are refused by name. Sentence 2 - report description level-1 entries are not implicit redefinitions: the report binder never calls SetRedefinition. EDITIONS 2002/2014/2023 as before; the FD rule is COBOL-85 base language and the same binder arm serves 85.
